summary: Induction along the recursion of weightedSquareSum.

steps.lean: fun_induction F.weightedSquareSum k x j 1 <;> simp <;> unfold weightedSquareSum <;> simp_all
steps.claim: Induction following the definition of weightedSquareSum: for j ≥ ϱ + 1 it is 0 and both claims hold; for j < ϱ + 1 it is ∫ (weightedSquare(F, j, k, x, σg) + weightedSquareSum(F, k, x, j+1, σg)) dθ^F_j(σ).

steps.lean:
use fun s h g ↦ .trans (by simp) (lintegral_floorMeasure_mul_right le_top
    (by simp_all [hk.weightedSquare_invariant_support, hk.mono]) ⟨h, ⟨⟩⟩)
steps.claim: Invariance: for s ∈ Q_j, ∫ Φ(σsg) dθ^F_j(σ) = ∫ Φ(σg) dθ^F_j(σ) by lintegral_floorMeasure_mul_right (S = G_T), since Φ = weightedSquare + weightedSquareSum at j + 1 is left Q_{j+1}-invariant (weightedSquare_invariant_support and the induction hypothesis, via mono).

steps.lean:
grind [exists_ne_zero_of_ae F.ae_floorMeasure_mem, hk.weightedSquare_invariant_support.2, mono,
    add_zero, IsNear.of_floorGroup_mul]
steps.claim: Support: if weightedSquareSum(F, k, x, j, g) ≠ 0, then for some σ ∈ H_j (θ^F_j-a.e.) the integrand at σg is nonzero, so σg is near at j + 1 (both terms vanish off such points), hence g is near at j (IsNear.of_floorGroup_mul).
